\subsection*{Turing Machine --- Oracle Finite: Introduction}

Declarations of the Lean module \texttt{TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.OracleFinite}.

\subsection*{Turing Machine --- Oracle Finite: Results}

\begin{definition}[Finite oracle Turing machine]
\lean{Turing.FinOracleTM}
\statementsource{BGS75}{
  pdf-2459e3840724-p002-b001,
  pdf-2459e3840724-p002-b002
}
\label{Turing.FinOracleTM}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.OracleTM, Turing.OracleTM.WellFormed}
For a symbol alphabet, a finite oracle Turing machine consists of a nonnegative number
$k$ of ordinary work tapes, a finite state set with decidable equality, and an oracle
Turing machine with those parameters whose query state and two answer states are
pairwise distinct.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Time-bounded oracle computation]
\lean{Turing.FinOracleTM.ComputesInTime}
\label{Turing.FinOracleTM.ComputesInTime}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinOracleTM, Turing.OracleTM.ComputesInTime}
Let $M$ be an oracle Turing machine, let $O$ be an oracle language, and let $x$ and $y$
be input and output words. For a nonnegative integer $t$, $M$ computes $y$ on input $x$
within $t$ steps relative to $O$ if its configuration after exactly $t$ steps has halted
and its output tape contains exactly $y$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Time-bounded decision by an oracle machine]
\lean{Turing.FinOracleTM.DecidesInTime}
\label{Turing.FinOracleTM.DecidesInTime}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinOracleTM, Turing.FinOracleTM.ComputesInTime, Turing.MultiTapeTM.indicator}
Let $M$ be a finite oracle Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, let $O$ and $L$ be
languages of Boolean words, and let $T$ assign a nonnegative integer to each nonnegative
integer. For every Boolean word $x$, the machine with oracle $O$ halts after exactly
$T(|x|)$ steps and outputs the one-symbol word whose symbol is true exactly when $x\in
L$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Monotonicity of computation time]
\lean{Turing.FinOracleTM.ComputesInTime.mono}
\label{Turing.FinOracleTM.ComputesInTime.mono}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinOracleTM, Turing.FinOracleTM.ComputesInTime, Turing.OracleTM.ComputesInTime.mono}
\difficulty{1}
Let $M$ be a finite-state deterministic oracle Turing machine, let $O$ be an oracle
language, and let $x,y$ be words over its alphabet. If $M$ on input $x$ with oracle $O$
halts with output $y$ after $t$ steps, then it does so after every $t'\ge t$ steps.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Uniqueness of computed output]
\lean{Turing.FinOracleTM.ComputesInTime.output_unique}
\label{Turing.FinOracleTM.ComputesInTime.output_unique}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinOracleTM, Turing.FinOracleTM.ComputesInTime, Turing.OracleTM.ComputesInTime.output_unique}
\difficulty{1}
Let $M$ be a finite-state deterministic oracle Turing machine, let $O$ be an oracle
language, and let $x,w,w'$ be words over its alphabet. If $M$ on input $x$ with oracle
$O$ halts with output $w$ after $t$ steps and also halts with output $w'$ after $t'$
steps, then $w=w'$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Embedding a finite machine as an oracle machine]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.toFinOracleTM}
\label{Turing.FinTM.toFinOracleTM}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinOracleTM, Turing.FinTM, Turing.OracleTM.ofMultiTapeTM, Turing.OracleTM.ofMultiTapeTM_wellFormed}
Let $M$ be a finite deterministic Turing machine over a symbol alphabet. Its associated
finite oracle Turing machine has the same number of ordinary work tapes, state set
enlarged by three additional states, and underlying oracle machine obtained from $M$ by
the standard conversion from a deterministic machine to an oracle machine.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Oracle compilation preserves computation time]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.toFinOracleTM_computesInTime}
\label{Turing.FinTM.toFinOracleTM_computesInTime}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinOracleTM.ComputesInTime, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime, Turing.FinTM.computesInTime_iff, Turing.FinTM.toFinOracleTM, Turing.OracleTM.computesInTime_ofMultiTapeTM}
\difficulty{3}
Let $M$ be a finite Turing machine over an alphabet $\Sigma$, let $O$ be a language over
$\Sigma$, and let $x,y\in\Sigma^*$ and $t\in\mathbb{N}$. The oracle machine associated
with $M$ computes $y$ from $x$ relative to $O$ in exactly $t$ steps if and only if $M$
computes $y$ from $x$ within $t$ steps.
\end{theorem}
